misconceptions.description: Presenting passion for technology in place of tool choices reasoned against real constraints
misconceptions.trigger: presentation uses words like passionate or transform with no constraint reasoning
misconceptions.feedback: Show a tool choice reasoned against the placement constraint that actually mattered, not enthusiasm.

misconceptions.description: Describing the ideal tool setting and never showing how the judgment transfers to a constrained classroom
misconceptions.trigger: presenter restates the ideal when asked how the vision fits a limited school
misconceptions.feedback: Show how the underlying judgment adapts to the new constraint set, not that the ideal is repeated.

misconceptions.description: Using AI to supply the professional vision or invent evidence rather than to pressure-test the candidate's own
misconceptions.trigger: presenter relies on a model to author the vision or fabricate placement data
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI to rehearse hard questions; the vision and its evidence must be your own.

misconceptions.description: Claiming an approach works in any classroom rather than naming its boundary conditions
misconceptions.trigger: presenter states the approach fits all settings with no exceptions
misconceptions.feedback: Name settings where the approach would not fit and what you would do instead; limits build credibility.
